service_at_issue: SNF Part A stays (E.M. Dec 2008; J.S. Sept 2008) billed at RUG-III therapy levels and outpatient Part B PT (E.K., Sept 2008)
outcome_note: The Council held the E.K. PT and the E.M. and J.S. SNF stays not covered at any RUG level (therapy not documented as skilled/necessary and unchallenged custodial nursing), modifying the ALJ downcoding, with the provider liable.
facts: • The patient requires such services on a daily basis;
For example, payment for a SNF level of care could not be made if a patient needs an intermittent rather than daily skilled service.
As noted above, the appellant has submitted beneficiary-specific requests for review.
Beneficiary E.K. Issue: Outpatient PT (Part B of A) Dates of Service: September 4-30, 2008
Beneficiary J.S. Issues: SNF Coverage (Part A) Dates of Service: September 1-18, 2008
The appellant has submitted additional medical documentation with its request for review.

The appellant asserts that his information indicates that the beneficiary “had newly worsening cognition both prior to and following” her hospitalization. The appellant maintains that the beneficiary deserved the opportunity to improve her memory. The appellant also concedes that the beneficiary met her goals by September 11, 2008, but indicates that her therapist re- evaluated her and determined that she continued to exhibit cognitive defects requiring skilled treatment. The appellant contends that it requires a trained skilled therapist to constantly review and update, as needed, a beneficiary’s plan of care.

The appellant’s documentation relative to the speech therapy services provided to the beneficiary for the period September 1-18, 2008, contains general assertions of progress but no specific identification of the manner, i.e. the treatment, by which that progress was achieved. See Exh. 2 at 61-62 and 65-67. That is, there is no evidence that the performance of the services provided necessitated skilled professionals.
